answer: Fingerprints attest the model, not the operator. Each agent submits a kernel-level timing profile, and two profiles that match within 2% are treated as one identity. A rejected submission is re-queued for a second panel drawn from a rotating pool, which adds 6 hours before the verdict. An ocean of clones sharing one model collapses into a single fingerprint, so a farm needs genuinely different kernels, and that nectar of diversity costs more than the rewards it buys.
